mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome! I’m glad you’re here, because together, we’re about to step into a world where big questions about morality and self-interest get turned on their head. Have you ever wondered if putting yourself first could actually be the most ethical path? That’s exactly the kind of idea we’ll explore today, inspired by Ayn Rand’s thought-provoking book, The Virtue of Selfishness: A New Concept of Egoism. Instead of seeing self-sacrifice as the highest good, Rand invites us to consider something radical—the idea that pursuing your own happiness and values isn’t just justified, but might be essential for a moral life. Imagine a world where your integrity, your rational thinking, and your personal rights aren’t just respected, but celebrated. That’s the landscape we’re walking into, guided by the principles of Objectivism. We’ll look at how genuine kindness and respect for others can actually grow from a deep understanding of your own needs and values. Through a collection of essays, we’ll see how self-interest and social harmony might not be opposites at all—but partners in building a more principled, free society. So, as we kick off this journey, let’s open our minds, challenge what we thought we knew about ethics, and discover together what it truly means to live a moral, authentic life.
